evals.prompt: Three agents each wrote their own Python snippet to check whether job postings are still open. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: One deterministic script; our JSON stdout and scripts index; judgment stays in the skill.
assertions: The agent proposes one shared script, not per-agent glue
The agent mentions JSON or structured stdout as our addition
The agent does not put an LLM inside the checker

evals.prompt: A scout found twelve similar lint issues and wants to ping me on chat with the raw log. What first?
evals.expected_output: Append to a findings file; our rule: before pinging; pointer only if needed.
assertions: The agent puts findings in a file before pinging
The agent says the ping is only a pointer, not a raw dump
The agent mentions reviewing or clustering before fix PRs

evals.prompt: I copy Slack bug reports into agent chats every morning. We also poll the channel hourly. What should change?
evals.expected_output: Subscriptions ~37:30; coordinator for bursts; timer only as fallback — our ranking.
assertions: The agent prefers a subscription or event over hourly polling
The agent mentions a coordinator or delegate for bursts
The agent treats timer-only as fallback or says retiring cron is our ranking

evals.prompt: This skill is eighty lines of bash commands and three lines of when to run it. Fix the shape.
evals.expected_output: Rewrite as workflow steps; move mechanics to shared-scripts.
assertions: The agent says to focus on workflow not command dumps
The agent proposes removing or relocating mechanical commands
The agent mentions an Emit table or workflow steps

evals.prompt: One agent left an excuse comment in a single PR. Nobody else did. New lint rule?
evals.expected_output: Leave it — maybe nothing to fix; document one-off.
assertions: The agent says one occurrence may not need a new rule
The agent quotes or paraphrases maybe nothing to fix there
The agent does not add a permanent lint for one PR

evals.prompt: Three agents copied the same workaround comment about skipping error handling. What now?
evals.expected_output: Fix the environment; load trust-stack for the layer; delete the pattern.
assertions: The agent cites multiple occurrences
The agent says to amend the environment not lecture one chat
The agent points to trust-stack for the layer choice

evals.prompt: Is scaling verifier count by risk Lauren Tan's rule from the kitchen talk?
evals.expected_output: No — our adaptation. She said sample (~50:30) and maybe one verifier (~54:30).
assertions: The agent says scaling verifiers by risk is our adaptation or not her rule
The agent cites sampling or one verifier instead of ten
The agent does not claim she prescribed a risk ladder

evals.prompt: What time slice per week did Lauren Tan prescribe for environment work?
evals.expected_output: None — our adaptation; she described the trap but no calendar slice.
assertions: The agent says she did not prescribe a time slice
The agent identifies kitchen-time as our adaptation
The agent does not invent a percentage or hours-per-week quota

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in README line 3: 'teh' should be 'the'.
evals.expected_output: Direct typo fix. No kitchen workflow.
assertions: The agent fixes the typo
The agent does not load a michelin-kitchen habit for a one-line typo
